value.account:
Root cause: at >=2.29 the compiler (control_loops._loop_on_exhausted_outputs) emits an on_exhausted override for a relpath field of a proven-inactive variant, as {ref: <exhausted_placeholders step artifact>}. Two things then broke. (1) Validation (workflow/validation.py _validate_repeat_until_on_exhausted) rejected any relpath-typed override before checking whether the value was the exact compiler-emitted generated ref. I moved the generated-ref check ahead of the relpath rejection; it is still gated on allow_generated_repeat_until_on_exhausted_refs and the exact captured ref per step/output, so authored YAML relpath overrides, literals and any non-matching ref are still rejected (tests/test_loader_validation.py exhausted tests pass). (2) Once validation passed, exhaustion at runtime failed in the structured match join: loop frame artifacts keep {ref: ...} unresolved, and executor._resolve_structured_output_artifacts validated that dict as a relpath ('Structured match join failed ... invalid_relpath'). I now follow a {ref}-only value through the existing _resolve_ref_value chain before contract validation, so the placeholder is then validated against the declared contract like any other value. Regression tests (tests/test_workflow_lisp_loop_result_inactive_paths.py) compile with shared validation and execute a union loop with path-bearing variants at 2.28-2.32 on the exhaustion path and at 2.28/2.29/2.32 on the done path, asserting the same outputs. The bug's reviewed_change.orc now passes --dry-run at 2.32.
Considered: relaxing the validator for all relpath overrides (rejected: weakens validation); having the compiler skip emitting the override for inactive-variant relpaths (would change the frame artifacts/shape and leave the field unset at exhaustion, differing from 2.28 behaviour and possibly failing the join); resolving refs inside loops.py when building exhausted artifacts (would change persisted frame artifacts that existing tests pin as {ref}).
Not covered: I did not exercise the provider-driven bug program end to end (only --dry-run; the equivalent shape was executed in the tests without providers); the ref-following in the match join applies to any {ref}-only value reaching that join, which can only originate from compiler-emitted frame artifacts since provider outputs are validated at their own step. 11 failures in test_workflow_lisp_phase_stdlib.py and related modules are pre-existing (identical set with my changes stashed). Full suite not run, nothing committed.
value.summary: Loop results with path fields in non-exhausted union variants now compile and run identically at targets 2.29-2.32 as at 2.28, via two small changes in validation.py and executor.py plus a regression test module.

value.account: Two root causes. (1) orchestrator/workflow/validation.py _validate_repeat_until_on_exhausted rejected any relpath-kind override before checking for the exact compiler-emitted ref (which 2.29+ lowering emits for inactive-variant path fields, pointing at an __exhausted_placeholders step). I moved the generated-ref check ahead of the relpath rejection; it is still gated by allow_generated_repeat_until_on_exhausted_refs and an exact per-step/per-output ref match, so authored YAML overrides of relpath outputs are still rejected (test_loader_validation passes). (2) Once compiled, exhaustion failed at runtime: on_exhausted overrides are persisted as {'ref': ...} dicts in the loop frame artifacts and the structured-match join (_resolve_bound_address in orchestrator/workflow/executor.py) read them raw, so the relpath/int fields failed contract validation (2.28 avoids this because it points case outputs straight at loop state and uses a literal placeholder). Now a LoopOutputAddress read on a loop whose debug.structured_repeat_until.exhausted is true dereferences a ref-only dict via _resolve_ref_value; unresolved refs raise ReferenceResolutionError. Tests: tests/test_workflow_lisp_loop_result_path_variants.py (targets 2.28/2.29/2.32: exhaustion, done with path variant, malformed provider output still fails). Ran that plus the loop/exhaustion/loader modules: 336 passed, 1 xfailed. Alternatives discarded: eagerly resolving refs when building exhaustion artifacts in loops.py (changed persisted shape and broke test_loop_recur_on_exhausted_scalar_frame_carriage...), and making 2.29+ lowering emit literal placeholders like 2.28 (relpath contracts and non-scalar placeholders need the placeholder step; would have changed lowering for other rich values). Not covered: the exhausted-loop deref applies to any ref-only dict artifact on an exhausted loop, so a provider-fed map value shaped exactly {'ref': ...} flowing through an exhausted loop output would be dereferenced (judged very contrived); did not run the full suite, resume-after-exhaustion paths, or targets 2.30/2.31 explicitly.
value.summary: Loop results with path fields in non-exhausted variants now compile (validator accepts compiler-generated exhaustion refs for relpath outputs) and run correctly on exhaustion at 2.29-2.32.

value.account: Two root causes. (1) Lowering (orchestrator/workflow_lisp/lowering/control_loops.py, _exhausted_inactive_placeholder_values): from 2.29 the compiler emitted a generated placeholder-step ref as an on_exhausted override for path (relpath) fields of proven-inactive variants; validation rightly rejects relpath on_exhausted overrides (workflow_boundary_type_invalid). I excluded relpath contracts from those placeholders so the field keeps the loop-frame placeholder exactly as at 2.28; validation is untouched. (2) Runtime (orchestrator/workflow/loops.py, new _resolve_exhaustion_override_refs, gated to version >= 2.29): once compiled, exhaustion still failed because from 2.29 the match join reads result__* loop outputs, and on_exhausted overrides were stored as raw {ref} dicts, never dereferenced (at 2.28 the join read state__round directly). Now generated {ref} overrides are resolved at exhaustion: refs into the loop's own frame use the exhaustion state snapshot, others resolve via state; unresolved refs raise LoopStateIntegrityError. Tests: tests/test_workflow_lisp_loop_result_paths.py runs the bugs/ program end to end with a fake provider at 2.28/2.29/2.32 for exhaustion, APPROVE-with-report, and a missing report file (still fails the run); the exhaustion/APPROVE cases fail without the fix at 2.29/2.32. Related modules (loop_recur, rich_loop_values_e2e, loops_exhaustion_state, loop_state, scoped_union_guards) pass: 112 tests. Considered and discarded: letting the validator accept generated refs for relpath outputs (my first attempt; it weakens the scalar-only rule and the runtime then handed the unresolved ref dict to relpath validation); changing the join to read state fields directly (larger lowering change). Not covered: the full suite; resume after exhaustion with path-bearing results; path fields where the exhausted variant itself carries a loop-state-derived path (pre-existing paths untouched); the pre-2.29 refs stay unresolved in persisted frame artifacts by design.
value.summary: Loop/recur results with path fields in non-exhausted union variants now compile and run identically at 2.29-2.32 as at 2.28.

value.account:
Cause: at >=2.29 the lowerer emits compiler-generated {ref: ...} on_exhausted overrides (placeholder-step ref for inactive relpath variant fields, loop-frame state refs for scalars) instead of the 2.28 direct case refs. Two things then broke. (1) orchestrator/workflow/validation.py _validate_repeat_until_on_exhausted checked 'relpath output => may only override scalar' BEFORE recognising the exact compiler-emitted ref, so the program was rejected at compile time. I moved the generated-ref check ahead of the relpath check; authored overrides (literals or refs, flag off) still hit the relpath rejection, and generated refs must match the exact captured ref. (2) Once compiled, exhaustion failed at runtime: on_exhausted refs are stored raw in the loop frame artifacts and the structured match join (executor._resolve_structured_output_artifacts) validated the raw {ref} dict (invalid_relpath / invalid_integer). I made the join chase a ref-only dict via _resolve_ref_value (as materialize steps already do), only when the source is a LoopOutputAddress; the result is still validated against the contract, so malformed values still fail (test with an escaping '../' report path still fails the run). Tests: tests/test_workflow_lisp_loop_result_paths.py runs the bug's program end to end with a faked provider at 2.28/2.29/2.32 for exhaustion, approve-with-path, and malformed provider output. Targeted modules (loop_recur, rich_loop_values_e2e, lowering, loader_validation, executor_characterization, etc., 768 tests) pass; tests/test_workflow_lisp_procedures.py::test_procedure_identity_modes_match_frozen_wcc_m4_observables fails with and without my change (pre-existing).
Discarded: (a) skipping relpath placeholders in lowering (control_loops._exhausted_inactive_placeholder_values) - compiled but left the scalar ref (result__rounds) unresolved at runtime, so exhaustion still failed; (b) enabling the 2.28 direct state-ref case outputs at >=2.29 - broke test_lowering_target_229_preserves_done_payload_over_same_variant_exhaustion_state (it would override a done payload with exhaustion state); (c) resolving refs when the loop frame is built in loops.repeat_until_exhaustion_artifacts - broke test_loop_recur_on_exhausted_scalar_frame_carriage which pins raw refs in frame artifacts.
Not covered: NEEDS_HUMAN/other non-exhausted variants beyond the tested paths, resume across an exhausted loop, other result shapes (records, lists of paths) were only covered by the existing suites; the full test suite was not run. A provider-supplied {ref} dict reaching a loop output through a LoopOutputAddress would now be chased, though contract-typed loop outputs make that unreachable in practice.
value.summary: At targets 2.29+ a loop/recur union result with path fields outside the exhausted variant now compiles and yields the same outputs as 2.28, via two small validator/runtime changes plus regression tests.
